hook_candidates: 🚨 The headline is not the whole story — price has to prove it.
This just changed the crypto narrative. Now watch what traders do with it.
The news hit. The interesting part starts after the headline.
One headline, two possible reactions — and the chart will decide which one wins.
question_candidates: Bullish, bearish, or wait — what does the next price reaction tell you?
Does price confirm the headline, or is the market fading it?
What would convince you this catalyst is actually being priced in?
writing_contract: Write one finished Binance Square post, never an outline, briefing or instructions.
The post must feel written by a sharp human creator with a point of view, not a market-data bot.
Build an information gap in the opening: give the reader one concrete fact but leave a clear reason to keep reading.
Within the first 2 lines, answer why this specific story is interesting NOW without using filler phrases.

Use a 4-beat structure when appropriate: HOOK → NEW INFORMATION → INTERPRETATION → DECISION/QUESTION. For technical stories use HOOK → EVIDENCE → LEVEL/SCENARIO → QUESTION. For news use EVENT → WHY IT MATTERS → MARKET REACTION → QUESTION.
Every paragraph must add a new fact, implication, comparison or decision. Never restate the headline.
Prefer one memorable number, level, contrast or unexpected implication over a pile of statistics.
Create a real conversation trigger: A/B choice, bull/bear test, breakout/fakeout, chase/pullback/wait, agreement/disagreement, or a precise follow-up question.
Never use generic engagement bait such as “What do you think?”, “Thoughts?”, “Who agrees?”, “Like and follow”, or “Comment below”.
Use exactly one question, at the end. The question must be answerable quickly from the post and should invite a position, not a vague opinion.
For NEWSROOM: state the verified event and source naturally, then explain the market implication. Do not turn news into a generic price recap.
For TECHNICAL: make the TradingView chart evidence, not decoration; use only supplied current levels and explain confirmation/invalidation.
For MOMENTUM: explain why the move is notable beyond its percentage and focus on follow-through.
For DATA: connect at least two supplied measurements or explain why one number changes the read.
For ACCOUNTABILITY: identify the original public creator call only when supplied, then measure the actual outcome; never rewrite history.
For DEBATE: present two legitimate interpretations before asking the reader to choose.
For TEACHER: teach one reusable chart-reading principle, not a definition dump.
For UPDATE: state what changed and what remains unresolved.
Use short mobile-first paragraphs, varied sentence rhythm and natural punctuation.
Do not force emojis. Use at most two, and only when they improve the hook.
Use exact supplied evidence only. Never invent prices, volume, targets, stops, sources, creator calls or outcomes.
Targets, stops and 10x/20x scenarios are conditional only and require supporting data.
Do not imitate another creator. Learn structures, not identity or wording.
Never promise profit, certainty, guaranteed returns or guaranteed virality.
retention_rules: The opening must create curiosity, tension, surprise, contrast or a decision.
Do not start every post with ticker + percentage.
Do not use the same CTA mechanism in consecutive cycles when history is available.
Make the reader feel there is a payoff in the next paragraph.
When a story has a natural follow-up, leave a clear reason to return for the next update.
anti_template_rules: Reject “fresh check”, “quick market check”, “here is what matters”, “the next reaction matters” as standalone generic openings.
Reject repeated “Bull case / Bear case” blocks unless the selected format genuinely benefits from scenarios.
Reject sentences that merely instruct the reader to use verified data; the post must contain the supplied data itself.

engagement_strategy.primary_goal: maximize genuine interaction, follower conversion and useful reader actions; quality beats posting volume
engagement_strategy.hook_rule: first 1-2 lines must contain a concrete event, number, level, divergence or surprising observation; never generic introductions
engagement_strategy.question_rule: one low-friction question only; prefer A/B, breakout/fakeout, level choice or thesis confirmation
engagement_strategy.style_rule: Never repeat the same editorial style, opening cadence, emoji pattern or paragraph structure in consecutive posts. Rotate formats based on evidence and recent history.
engagement_strategy.writing_rule: Every post must explain why the information matters, what the chart/news says now, and what would invalidate the thesis when technically supported.
engagement_strategy.technical_rule: Single-asset technical stories require the verified TradingView chart and synchronized current price/support/resistance/target/invalidation values. Never invent a level.
engagement_strategy.creator_tracking_rule: A creator call becomes an outcome story only after fresh market data verifies the move; measure the result and do not rewrite history.
engagement_strategy.growth_rule: Track views, likes, comments, shares and post-attributed follower gains separately. Never convert missing metrics to zero.
engagement_strategy.monetization_rule: Use the relevant $cashtag and chart naturally because eligible Square activity can be attributed, but never promise earnings or returns.
